notes.CANDIDATE ending NOT triggered: RD-3 answers 'is ker partial = C^[3]?' YES, but the slice branch closes exactly, so no candidate isomorphism is assembled and the twin bar is not invoked. Nothing about X x A^1 = A^4 in general is claimed or implied: what closes is the route THROUGH THIS FLOW's slice.
notes.criterion: a slice is s with partial_red(s) = 1 (partial itself is excluded a priori: RD-2 showed partial(A[w]) is inside t^3 A[w]). ker(partial_red) = ker(partial) = C[p,q,t], so a slice would give A[w] = C[p,q,t][s] = C^[4].
notes.every component of partial_red vanishes: so partial_red(F)(origin) = 0 for EVERY F, by the chain rule
notes.failure locus against the RD-4 divisor: the degeneracy locus lives on {t = 0}; the localisation theorem makes A[w][1/(t(p+1))] = C[p,q,t][1/(t(p+1))][Z] with Z = z+xw. So the slice exists after inverting t(p+1) and the whole failure is concentrated on that one divisor of A^3 = Spec(ker partial).
notes.partial_red has NO SLICE: exact, unconditional, no degree cap: partial_red(A[w]) is contained in the maximal ideal of the origin, and 1 is not.
notes.search measurement: linear (exact Q nullspace), not an elimination: [6, 21, 56] unknowns at degrees [1, 2, 3]. Agrees with the theorem, which needs no cap.
notes.structural route: a slice would force a: A[w] = ker[s] makes Ga act by translation, hence freely; but RD-4 exhibits the fixed line {x=z=t=w=0}

ending.scope: This says nothing about the Zariski cancellation question itself. It closes one explicit route and replaces it with a sharper, bounded one (the localisation theorem's divisor).

exact_theorem.proof_1: every component of partial_red vanishes at the origin of X x A^1; by the chain rule so does partial_red(F) for every F; 1 does not.
exact_theorem.proof_2: a slice makes A[w] = (ker partial)[s], so the Ga-action is a translation and therefore free; RD-4 exhibits a whole line of fixed points.
exact_theorem.status: EXACT THEOREM -- not a cap-limited search
exact_theorem.verdict: partial_red (hence partial) admits NO SLICE on A[w]

failure_locus.slice_after_localisation: Z = z + x w, partial_red(Z) = t^3(p+1)
